newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift down on low Western support.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift down on low Western support.

text.p: Leading Russian shares drifted down on Tuesday on low Western support and quiet trading, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 shares slipped by 0.62 percent to 320.33 on low total market volume of $28.21 million in volume.
"All orders have been fulfilled, a correction has taken place," said UFG trader Maxim Perlin. "Now the market is slipping slowly due to uncertainty."
Traders said there was a fall in leading shares, while other prices remain on unchanged levels.
Utility UES fell to $0.2160 from $0.2190 at Monday's close, utility Irkutskenergo slipped to $0.253 from $0.263, Surgutneftegaz oil company was $0.801 after $0.815.
Traders said Western investors did not participate in trading waiting for lower price levels.
"Many people are either waiting for a deeper fall, or stronger fluctuations," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell co-head of equity trading Pavel Gronbjerg.
Traders forecast a quiet market this week, but said that low sales volumes from the West testified to the fact that the quietness would not last long.

"People are taking profits little by little, but Western clients are not taking part in this as they do not think the correction will last long," said Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov.
